messages:
maya: Morning — kicking off a quick sync for LedgersEdge week0 private/VPC onboarding. Summary: networking test to priv-redwood-api:8443 failing from their transit gateway, KMS key policy missing cross-account role permissions, and they asked about Dedicated pricing/renewal options. Can SRE/security pair on network + KMS?

ravi-ledgers: Hey all — confirmed we cannot curl https://priv-redwood-api:8443 from our TGW vpc-ldg-1. TCP RST after SYN. We can reach other endpoints in the VPC. We also tried a NAT instance, still no dice.

devon: @maya thanks. Can you paste the traceroute and SG/route table IDs? quick guess: missing route from TGW attachment to priv subnet or a blackhole on the egress ACL.

ravi-ledgers: traceroute attached (pasted):
1 10.0.0.1
2 10.10.0.5
3 * * *
4 * * *

SGs: sg-0a1b2c3d (app), route table rtb-0f1e2d3c.

devon: Looks like packets never hit the env-facing ELB. Can you run `curl -v --resolve priv-redwood-api:8443:10.20.30.40 https://priv-redwood-api:8443/health` from an instance in the TGW VPC and paste stdout? also confirm TGW route table has a route to 10.20.30.0/24 via the attachment.

ravi-ledgers: ran the curl: `* Connected to priv-redwood-api (10.20.30.40) port 8443 (#0)` then `* Received HTTP/1.1 403` — so different behavior from the traceroute. We do see 403 when resolving to internal IP, but direct DNS gives RST earlier.

anika: Two things: 1) 403 implies a TLS or app-level reject (maybe missing client cert or IP allowlist). 2) For the KMS, Ravi — can you share the key ARN? We need to confirm the key policy includes `arn:aws:iam::REDCOMPANY:role/redwood-inference-priv-role` with Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey permissions.

ravi-ledgers: KMS key arn: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345. Policy currently only allows their account principal, not cross-account roles.

anika: Suggested policy snippet (place in their key policy or create a grant):
```
{
  "Sid": "AllowRedwoodPrivRole",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::987654321098:role/redwood-inference-priv-role"},
  "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:DescribeKey"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```
Add `kms:ReEncrypt*` if you plan rotation flows.

devon: For the network/DNS oddness — sounds like their public DNS is resolving to an ILB edge IP that is not routable from TGW. Recommend they add a private hosted zone entry pointing priv-redwood-api -> 10.20.30.40 in their account, or attach the VPC endpoint we provided. If they prefer not to touch DNS, we can supply an override on our side via peering but that's slower.

ravi-ledgers: We can add a private hosted zone. Quick Q: will that block your external monitoring? we need health checks working from Redwood.

maya: We can run monitoring from inside our peering attachment if you add the private hosted zone and the route. Ops note: we need two things before we mark week0 green — 1) successful 5-min sustained health checks from Redwood probes, 2) KMS grant or policy in place.

infra-bot: deploy-checker: priv-edge-probe job ran at 2026-03-23T09:12:45Z — result: FAIL (tcp timeout). See logs: https://internal.redwood/probes/1831234567

devon: Action: Ravi -> create private hosted zone + add A record to 10.20.30.40; add route in TGW route table to 10.20.30.0/24. Anika -> draft KMS policy snippet + send to Ravi for approval. Maya -> schedule 30-min joint verification tomorrow 09:00 PT.

ravi-ledgers: Doing hosted zone now, will post when done. Also asked our security team to approve the KMS snippet — they may prefer an IAM grant instead.

anika: IAM grant also OK, but ensure the grant includes `EncryptionContext` caveats if you use them. If they need a template, I can drop a grant CLI example.

devon: For the short-term workaround, if they want to demo, we can open the ingress SG to their TGW-originating IP range and bypass DNS — but that's ephemeral.

ravi-ledgers: Hosted zone created and A record added. Route updated (rtb-0f1e2d3c now points 10.20.30.0/24 -> tgw-attach-0aa).

infra-bot: deploy-checker: re-run at 2026-03-23T09:45:02Z — result: PASS (HTTP 200 /health).

devon: Nice. Maya — can you confirm with Ravi that logs show our probe traffic and there are no 403s?

ravi-ledgers: Logs show 200 responses to our internal IPs. KMS policy still pending; security asked for grant example.

anika: Grant CLI example: `aws kms create-grant --key-id abcd-ef01-2345 --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::987654321098:role/redwood-inference-priv-role --operations Encrypt Decrypt GenerateDataKey` — include `--constraints` if needed. Sending to Ravi in DM.

maya: Notes for playbook/feedback capture: customer requested clearer default runbook for KMS onboarding (policy vs grant pros/cons) and a one-page networking checklist (DNS, TGW routes, SGs, healthcheck IPs). Also flagged potential renewal interest for Dedicated in ~6 months; mark as low->med risk/opportunity and loop in Simon from sales.

simon-sales: Thanks @maya — I'll reach out to Ravi for a Dedicated intro and set a calendar for exploratory pricing. Maya, can you add a short note with projected consumption so I can pre-populate options?

maya: Will do. Action items summary: 1) Ravi — confirm KMS grant/policy decision and apply. 2) Devon/Anika — help validate policy/grant and run verification. 3) Maya — create two one-pagers (KMS onboarding runbook + private networking checklist) and send to Ravi. 4) Simon — outreach on Dedicated options.

ravi-ledgers: Thanks all — will update when KMS grant is applied. Appreciate the quick turnaround! :thumbsup:
